title: EaseMyTrip Gives Hero Flydubai Pilot Free Domestic Flights for Five Years
excerpt: After Capt Smit Machchhar was stabbed by his co-pilot on Flydubai flight FZ1073 and helped save 170+ lives, EaseMyTrip announced free domestic travel for him, his wife and children for five years.
body:
• EaseMyTrip will give Indian pilot Capt Smit Machchhar — stabbed by his co-pilot on Flydubai flight FZ1073 on September 30 — free domestic air travel in India for five years, covering his wife and children too.
  • Machchhar, seriously injured in the attack, helped prevent the apparent hijacking attempt of the Dubai–Tel Aviv flight carrying more than 170 people; he remains in stable condition at a hospital in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
  • Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed Machchhar as a "HERO" on X, saying his valour "helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy," while Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu called him a "true hero."
  • EaseMyTrip CEO Rikant Pittie said the gesture reflects the company's belief that "when one of our own stands strong for the nation, we must stand with them and their family."

Five Years of Free Flights for a Pilot's Courage

Online travel agency EaseMyTrip has announced it will offer Indian pilot Capt Smit Machchhar — and his wife and children — complimentary domestic air travel across India for the next five years, honouring the commercial pilot whose actions helped foil an apparent hijacking attempt aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073 on September 30.

"Captain Smit Machchhar's courage, composure and presence of mind in an extraordinary situation are qualities every Indian can take pride in," said Rikant Pittie, the company's CEO and co-founder, in a statement shared with HT Lifestyle. "As a humble gesture of gratitude, we are pleased to offer Captain Machchhar, his wife and children complimentary domestic air travel across India for the next five years."

"In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others. His valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy."

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on X

Context & Background

Machchhar was flying FZ1073 from Dubai International Airport to Ben Gurion Airport in Israel when, about two and a half hours after take-off, he was reportedly stabbed by his co-pilot in an alleged attempt to crash the aircraft. The plane, carrying more than 170 people, went into a rapid descent over Saudi Arabia, dropping more than 17,000 feet in under two minutes. After briefly entering Jordanian airspace, it looped back and landed in Saudi Arabia.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later confirmed that one pilot had stabbed the other before apparently trying to crash the plane. An Israeli passenger told Netanyahu the plane "went into a spin and began to descend" before the passenger and a crew member broke into the cockpit and overpowered the attacker. Machchhar was taken to a hospital in Tabuk, in north-western Saudi Arabia, where the Indian embassy in Riyadh says he remains in stable condition.

Impact & Analysis

The accolades have come from the highest levels. Netanyahu called Machchhar a "true hero," and global leaders and diplomats have lined up to praise him. Modi's X post — calling him "HERO" in capital letters — framed the incident as a matter of national pride: "India is proud of Captain Machchhar. Praying for his speedy recovery, renewed strength and good health."

EaseMyTrip's offer is the first major corporate recognition of the pilot's actions, and it is calibrated precisely to his situation: a commercial pilot, recovering from stab wounds in a Saudi hospital, offered the simplest gift an Indian travel company can give — the freedom to fly home, and to travel the country he helped make proud, with his family. The five-year term gives the gesture weight beyond a one-off headline.

Diaspora Angle

For the diaspora, Machchhar's story has landed with particular force. Thousands of Indian pilots fly for Gulf carriers — Flydubai, Emirates, Qatar Airways, Etihad — and many diaspora families in the UAE personally know someone in an Emirates or flydubai cockpit. The thought of an Indian captain attacked in his own cockpit, on a route diaspora travellers fly regularly between the Gulf and Tel Aviv, feels close. The heroism narrative has also resonated across continents precisely because it inverts the usual aviation-safety story: this time, the threat was not mechanical failure or weather, but a human one — and it was met with composure that saved more than 170 lives.

What's Next

The investigation into the attack is ongoing, and the co-pilot's motives remain unclear. Machchhar's recovery in Tabuk will determine his return to flying. For now, the aviation world is watching to see what recognition follows from regulators and airlines — and whether other companies follow EaseMyTrip's lead in honouring the pilot.
nri_angle: Thousands of Indian pilots fly for Gulf carriers, so the attack on Capt Machchhar in a flydubai cockpit on a Gulf–Tel Aviv route hits close to diaspora families in the UAE; his heroism has resonated globally as a story of composure saving 170+ lives.
